text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The cabinet on Wednesday directed Youth and Sports Minister Muhyiddin Yassin to take on the leading role of ensuring the smooth organisation of the 1998 Commonwealth Games scheduled for September 11-21 next year.
-- Contractors who damage utility cables during digging works may be held accountable for the entire consequence of the disruption and not just the cost of repairing the cables.
-- The cabinet decided on Wednesday that rap group KRU be allowed to hold its nationwide concert tour.
-- Timbermaster Industries Bhd is believed to have secured the rights to log timber on a million-hectare site in Gabon recently in its continuing expansion drive into Africa.
-- Ekran Bhd has cancelled the proposed Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd one-for-one rights issue exercise which was earlier scheduled to be completed before January 1, 1999.
-- Malaysia has been singled out by the International Moneray Fund for its ability to manage its success.
-- Malayan Banking Bhd has been named the most preferred bank for raising capital by Malaysian corporate entities in a poll conducted by Asiamoney.
